name: Naturalisation via Marriage to a Bulgarian Citizen

qualifying_event.description: Marriage to a Bulgarian citizen does NOT change the foreign spouse's citizenship automatically (Citizenship Act Article 5). It instead reduces the residence bar for standard naturalisation from 5 to 3 years of permanent residence, provided the marriage has also lasted at least 3 years.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage certificate; proof of at least 3 years of permanent residence and 3 years of marriage.

requirements.blocker_text: Must be legally married to a Bulgarian citizen for at least 3 years (Citizenship Act Article 13). Available equally regardless of the spouse's or applicant's sex -- the Act does not distinguish by gender.

Requires 3 years holding PERMANENT residence status (reduced from the standard route's 5 years), which itself requires prior years of long-term residence to obtain -- this is a reduced naturalisation bar, not an accelerated marriage-only grant.
requirements.fix_path: Hold permanent residence status continuously for 3 years while married to a Bulgarian citizen.

sources.title: Bulgaria -- Bulgarian Citizenship Act, Article 5 (marriage does not automatically change citizenship) and Article 13 (reduced 3-year-permanent-residence naturalisation bar for those married 3+ years to a Bulgarian citizen)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Bulgaria). Unlike some countries in this dataset with a genuinely gender-restricted or near-automatic marriage-to-citizenship grant, Bulgaria's marriage route is gender-neutral but is really just a REDUCED naturalisation threshold (3 years permanent residence + 3 years marriage, vs. the standard 5 years permanent residence) -- not a fast automatic grant. dual_citizenship_allowed modeled FALSE for consistency with bg_naturalisation.json's standard route, since Article 13 does not appear to exempt this route from Article 12's prior-citizenship-release condition; this was not explicitly re-confirmed for Article 13 specifically and is flagged as an inference from the general naturalisation renunciation rule.
